report: console proof stdout-only uname grouping: independent quick review
verdict: SOUND. Grouping the uname commands under '{ uname -s; uname -m; uname -r; } 2>/dev/null' removes only uname stderr from the console. The strict stdout response pattern is unchanged and nothing is filtered, so suppression can only cause false negatives, never a pass.
context: attempt-008 reached a real M1 shell (fresh nonce-joined response 'Darwin arm64 25.5.0', no panic). The original strict checker rejected it because six nonfatal uname malloc stderr lines interleaved with stdout. The original 008 receipts and source snapshots are preserved and are being audited separately by Astra.

findings.fact: Host ConsoleProof.command() and the controller's console_observation() expected bytes both contain '{ uname -s; uname -m; uname -r; } 2>/dev/null;'. The POSIX brace group (spaces and terminating ';' correct; valid in sh/bash/zsh/dash, not csh) redirects only fd 2 of the uname commands; the printf markers and stdout are unaffected.

The strict pattern is byte-identical in host and controller: after CR removal, 
DL9_BEGIN_<nonce>
Darwin
arm64
[0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.+-]{0,100}
DL9_END_<nonce>
. No warning or line filtering was added.

Fail-safe: a missing uname, missing /dev/null (a redirection failure skips the group) or a uname error produces no Darwin/arm64 stdout, so the strict match fails. The suppressed stderr can hide diagnostics but cannot create a pass.

Echo resistance unchanged: the command still splits the nonce into two quoted literals (the full nonce never appears contiguously in the input; test-asserted) and contains no '\nDarwin\narm64' sequence.

Recommended tests now present (added by root after final009 had launched; no hardware changed after launch): an interleaved stderr-line negative in BOTH suites (test_host_progress.py:212, tests/test_m1_bringup_cycle.py:105, 'uname(1) malloc: diagnostic must not be filtered' between Darwin and arm64 must fail) and cross-module input equality (tests/test_m1_bringup_cycle.py:83, controller expected bytes == ConsoleProof(nonce).command()).
Independent reruns: test_host_progress.py 18/18 OK; tests.test_m1_bringup_cycle 6/6 OK. The new assertions extend existing test methods, so the counts are unchanged.

notes: The new controller rejects attempt-008's original challenge bytes by design ('Unexpected challenge bytes'). Audit 008 only with its own per-attempt saved controller/helper source; do not re-verdict it with the new controller.

The six malloc warnings are a real userspace symptom, now excluded from the proof only. They remain in the raw 008 console; track them separately (for example a later unredirected diagnostic uname outside the proof).
